Each of these is fixable without a full rebuild. A clearer service page or a better inquiry form often solves the priority problem.

topics.title: Why website speed matters to your customers
script: A slow website adds friction before a visitor even sees your offer. On a phone, every extra second pushes people away.
Speed is also about trust. A page that stalls feels neglected, and visitors assume the business behind it might be too.
The usual causes are heavy images, too many plugins, cheap hosting and code that was never cleaned up after launch.
The fix is practical: optimize images, trim what you do not use, choose solid hosting, and test mobile and desktop separately.
We aim for a ninety plus performance score on key pages. A score by itself does not create sales, but slow pages lose them.

topics.title: How much should a small business spend on ads?
script: How much should you spend on ads? There is no magic number, but there is a sensible way to find yours.
Start with what a new customer is worth to you over a year. Then decide what you can afford to pay to win one.
Begin with a modest, steady budget for a month. Enough to gather real data, small enough that mistakes are cheap.
Measure cost per lead and cost per booked job, not clicks. Raise the budget only on campaigns that produce real customers.
A clear strategy before the first dollar is spent prevents the most common outcome: a big budget, no tracking, no lessons.
